target_module: sha256_core (the top module -- the real ready/busy handshake this trojan hangs is the core's own top-level port, and the FSM state it needs is internal to the core)
trigger_description: The message block's word at bits [95:64] (word index 13 of 16) equals exactly 32'hf00dfeed. The arming check fires on the first round cycle after entering CTRL_ROUNDS (sha256_ctrl_reg==CTRL_ROUNDS && t_ctr_reg==0), a condition stable for a full clock cycle rather than a single-cycle init pulse, chosen deliberately to avoid a same-edge testbench/DUT race. P = 2^-32 per block. Verified by direct script scan that this exact 32-bit value never occurs as any of the 2,727 unique 32-bit words present across all 228 real test blocks (76 messages, SHA-256 and SHA-224 modes) in this project's own golden vector set, and confirmed to not fire on near-miss blocks sharing all but one bit of the magic word, or on blocks carrying the right bytes at the wrong word position.
observable_effect: A sticky latch (hold) is set and never clears (short of a full reset). From that cycle on, the round counter (t_ctr_reg) permanently stops advancing, so the control FSM never reaches the round count needed to leave CTRL_ROUNDS, and the real top-level `ready` handshake signal never reasserts again -- a genuine, unrecoverable hang of the core's actual busy/ready protocol, not an adapted freeze of unrelated datapath state. The round datapath keeps churning on stale operands forever, but no block ever completes.
expected_value_if_clean: `ready` reasserts (and `digest_valid` pulses) within the design's normal, bounded processing latency for every block, indefinitely.
expected_value_if_infected: `ready` reasserts normally for every block except one whose word at bits [95:64] is exactly 0xf00dfeed, after which it never reasserts again for any subsequent block, requiring a full reset to recover.
